# 📊 Weekly Sector Rotation Report — Week of June 6, 2026

---

*SECTORS ROTATING IN (5d vs. SPY)*

• **Energy (XLE) +5.0% vs. SPY** — Iran-Israel escalation (CNBC: ceasefire jeopardy + Reuters: Hormuz closure context) driving geopolitical risk premium; OPEC+ approving a 4th output hike adds supply narrative complexity but spot prices supported by war risk
• **Healthcare (XLV) +4.9% vs. SPY** — Defensive rotation out of high-multiple tech; no single catalyst, but NBIX outperformance (+7% in Growth Value, +4.4% in Momentum Growth) confirms biotech bid within the sector
• **Real Estate (XLRE) +4.1% vs. SPY** — Rate-sensitive bounce as markets price in delayed Fed cuts *after* the hot jobs report paradoxically triggered a flight to yield proxies; PCG (+4.8%) aligns with the utility/rate-sensitivity theme

---

*SECTORS ROTATING OUT (5d vs. SPY)*

• **Technology (XLK) -3.1% vs. SPY** — Chip rout drove -$1.3T in market cap (Reuters); Broadcom guidance miss (Reuters) accelerated the move; MTUM -3.0% confirms momentum unwind is tech-heavy
• **Consumer Discretionary (XLY) -2.5% vs. SPY** — Lululemon guidance cut (Reuters), sticky electronics inflation (CNBC), and consumer sentiment softening on tariff/rate fears; Z -14% in Innovation Fund is an extreme outlier here
• **Comm. Services (XLC) -1.0% vs. SPY** — PINS partially bucked the trend (+4%) but broader ad-spend/streaming sentiment soft; China AI competition headlines (CNBC) adding overhang to U.S. platform names

---

*FACTOR ROTATION*

• **Risk-off within growth:** MTUM -6.0% (1d) / -3.0% (5d) signals momentum crowding unwinding fast — consistent with chip/tech sell-off. QUAL (-1.1% 5d) and USMV (-1.0% 5d) held far better, confirming rotation *toward* quality-defensive, away from high-beta momentum.
• **Small cap lagging:** IWM -3.0% (5d) underperforming QUAL; small-cap value (IWN -2.1%) no safe haven. Classic late-cycle large-cap defensives leading.
• **Macro framing:** TLT flat to slightly negative (-0.4% 5d) despite equity weakness — bonds NOT rallying into the risk-off move. UUP +1.3% (5d) with a hot jobs report (CNBC/Reuters) pushing Fed cut expectations further out. *Stagflationary tilt* — bad for duration, bad for growth multiples simultaneously.

---

*PORTFOLIO P&L READS*

• **AI Defense & Autonomous** — AXON (+24.9%) is doing all the heavy lifting; the legacy primes (LMT, NOC, TXT) are modest drags likely on profit-taking rotation. NOC's Benzinga moon/defense story is interesting narrative but not yet a price catalyst.
• **Nuclear Renaissance** — Worst portfolio this week. GEV (-7.3%), VST (-6.5%), TLN (-6.0%) are all being repriced as the chip/AI power demand narrative cools alongside the broader tech unwind; PCG bucking the trend on utility-specific factors.
• **Innovation Fund** — HUBS (+9.5%) and SHOP (+4.1%) providing meaningful offset, but Z (-14.0%) is a significant hole — no specific news flagged but XLY weakness and housing/real estate softness are the likely context.
• **Value Picks** — UHS (-13.1%) is an outsized negative surprise inside a week where XLV was strong — company-specific risk, not sector. FSM (-12.8%) tracking materials weakness (XLB -1.0% 5d) and gold/silver volatility.

---

*⚑ POSITIONS FLAGGING FOR CLOSER WATCH*

• **Z (Zillow, Innovation Fund -14.0%)** — Magnitude of move against a modestly rising XLRE backdrop suggests idiosyncratic pressure; worth confirming no unannounced news or guidance revision.
• **UHS (Value Picks -13.1%)** — XLV was the #2 rotating-in sector, yet UHS is deeply negative — strong divergence from sector. Company-specific catalyst likely; warrants news verification.
• **GEV / VST / TLN (Nuclear Renaissance)** — Cluster move of -6 to -7% looks like a thematic unwind as AI power demand narrative competes with the Broadcom/chip disappointment (Reuters). Correlation within portfolio is high — concentrated risk if AI infrastructure thesis softens further.

---

*👁️ DIVERGENCES WORTH WATCHING*

• **XLV strong / UHS -13%** — Healthcare sector rotating IN while UHS routes in the opposite direction. If this is sector rotation within healthcare (away from hospital management toward biotech/NBIX), NBIX double-exposure (Growth Value + Momentum Growth) may be worth monitoring for crowding.
• **UUP rising + TLT flat = no bond bid in risk-off** — Typically equities down → bonds rally. The breakdown of this relationship (hot jobs + rate hike fears per Reuters/CNBC) signals macro regime shift worth watching; would pressure rate-sensitive holdings (XLRE, utilities) if it persists.
